sections.facts: The Madhya Pradesh Government issued a notification prescribing the minimum rates of wages for employment in stone breaking and stone crushing operations carried on in mines, in exercise of the authority delegated to it by the President by a notification under article 258 of the Constitution. The appellant company, engaged in the manganese mining industry, challenged the validity of the said notification by a writ petition filed in the High Court. The High Court found against the appellant and rejected the petition.
sections.statute: Section 5(2) and Section 27 of the Act (II of 1948); Article 258 of the Constitution; Item 8 in Part 1 of the Schedule to the Act.
sections.argument: The appellant's case was that the said notification was ultra vires section 5(2) of the Act. The question for determination in the appeal was whether item 8 in Part 1 of the Schedule to the Act, properly construed, included stone breaking and stone crushing operations in a mining industry.
sections.analysis: The Court found that item 8 in Part 1 of the Schedule to the Act was not intended to cover the breaking or crushing of stones incidental to mining operations and must be limited to stone breaking and stone crushing employment in quarries. It would, however, be open to the Government, if it so desired, to achieve the object it had in view in issuing the impugned notification by adding appropriate items to the Schedule in exercise of its power under section 27 of the Act. It was further noted that it was not necessary for the appellant to challenge the vires of the Presidential notification in the first instance in order that he might impugn the notification in question (A. Thangal Kunju Musaliar vs M. Venkitachalam Potti, referred to).
sections.judgement: Held, that the impugned notification was ultra vires section 5(2) of the Act and could not be enforced.
